newsitem.title: USA: N. Korea meeting reset for Feb. 5 -U.S.
newsitem.headline: N. Korea meeting reset for Feb. 5 -U.S.

text.p: A briefing with North Korea on a proposal for Korean peninsula peace talks has been postponed until Feb. 5 in New York, the U.S. State Department said on Monday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the meeting was moved from Jan. 29 at Pyongyang's request because North Korea wanted to complete grain negotiations with a "private western company," presumably Cargill Inc.
"I could confirm that the North Koreans requested over the weekend that we postpone the joint briefing that we were to give on January 29 in New York City," Burns told reporters.

He said the United States and South Korea accepted the request and now "we plan to meet next week in New York on February 5 for a briefing on the four-party proposal that was made by (South Korean) President Kim (Young-sam) and President Clinton."

Burns said that in seeking the postponement, "The North Koreans mentioned to us...that they have put first priority recently on some grain discussions, discussions of the import of grain they're having...with some private Western companies. They want to conclude these negotiations. I guess they believe they can in the next week before they send their negotiators to New York for the briefing on February 5. That is a satisfactory explanation."

Burns did not specify any firm but the United States recently gave Minneapolis-based Cargill Inc. permission to export 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice to North Korea in what is expected to be a barter arrangement.
